A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RepTok research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet reconstruction and generation experiments, text-to-image evaluations on MS-COCO, and quantitative and qualitative ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds model-scaling, token-count, higher-resolution reconstruction and inference-timing results.

M1.justification: The proposed single-token adaptation, cosine regularization, flow-matching decoder and latent generators remain unchanged. V2 specifies a CFG interval but does not establish that it replaces a different v1 schedule. Larger models and additional register tokens are evaluated as experimental variants.

E1.justification: V2 adds a higher-resolution reconstruction scenario: Appendix B and Figure S6 demonstrate 512×512 reconstructions beyond v1's 256×256 experiments. ImageNet, COYO, MS-COCO and the main reconstruction, class-conditional and text-to-image tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The existing generation, reconstruction and interpolation comparator sets are retained. V2 adds an explicit inference-speed comparison against SiT-XL in new Table 5. Newly discussed RAE and SVG are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation with model-size and register-token controls, a 516M-parameter generator trained for 460K steps, and 100K-step fine-tuning at 512×512. Compute accounting now includes first-stage training, and Table 5 introduces component-level timing at specified NFE budgets. These are added configurations and evaluation procedures, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Figure 10 tests MLP-Mixer scaling, while Figure S7 compares the class token alone against adding one, two or four register tokens. These substantially extend analysis of capacity and the reconstruction-generation trade-off. Figure S6 adds a higher-resolution case study; existing backbone, regularization, interpolation and guidance analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bands. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces gFID 3.22 with 1.88, corresponding to the newly reported 516M-parameter variant; the earlier 276M model's 3.22 remains in v2 Table 2. Adding 30.4K PFLOPs of first-stage cost changes the 700K-step row's reported total from 4.1K to 34.5K PFLOPs through broader accounting. New scaling, token-count, reconstruction and timing outcomes substantially expand the evidence.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation, sampling description and cosine-regularization equations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: adapting a single SSL token for reconstruction, efficient latent generation and extension to text-to-image synthesis. New experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 explains poorer generation with extra register tokens through their lack of favorable semantic regularization and discusses the requirement for available non-spatial tokens. It also identifies the decoder as the dominant inference cost. The existing limitations concerning detail, compositional control and regularization are retained.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies CFG over t in [0.3, 0.9], component inference budgets, and initialization and training duration for 512×512 fine-tuning. It also documents first-stage compute and excluded shared pretraining costs. Appendix A's original implementation recipe and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds comparisons with concurrent RAE and SVG, distinguishing their spatial SSL representations from RepTok's pooled token. References to Kouzelis et al. and limited-interval guidance are also added. This extends the existing positioning without replacing its central framing.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. Changes include localized terminology and sentence edits, additional analysis paragraphs, conference headers, and correction of the supplementary title to match the paper.

P2.justification: The compute table is substantially expanded into first-stage, second-stage and total-cost columns. V2 adds scaling and token-count plots, a higher-resolution reconstruction panel and an inference table, and replaces Figure 6's sample display. Appendix figures are resized and rearranged; v1 Figures S6–S10 are retained as S8–S12.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency by exposing first-stage training costs omitted from v1's comparison table, and adds useful evidence about scaling and the single-token design. However, Section 4.1 retains the 1.7%-of-SiT efficiency statement without reconciling it with the expanded totals. The revision strengthens the paper's evidence and assessability, but only partly resolves its central efficiency-accounting weakness.
